name: Scanner_UI_Display
description: How scan results visually appear to the player: HUD overlay, world-space text, icons, scan progress indicator, targeting reticle, and knowledge-log integration.

questions.question: Does the UI present science as a natural readout (diegetic) rather than a textbook popup?
Can a 10-second GIF of the UI (crosshair on rock -> science panel) sell the game on Steam?
Does the scan result feel like an in-world instrument readout, not a menu screen?
Can the UI be built with existing UMG TextBlock + Image widgets without custom rendering?
Does the UI depend on any new widget framework or engine plugin?
Does the HUD approach work in UE5.8 without hacks (no Slate custom panels needed)?
Does the UI add measurable frame time (UMG text updates are near-free; what about scan-line overlay effects)?
Is the scan result readable for low-vision players (font size, contrast, screen-reader compat)?
Does the UI have audio accompaniment (scanning ping crescendo, result chime) synced to text reveal?
In co-op, can each player see their own scan results without cluttering the shared HUD?
Can modders customize the scan result panel layout, fonts, and colors through data files?
Is the UI layout flexible enough to accommodate text expansion (e.g., German noun-compounds)?
Does this depend on the main Educational_Scanner Scan() output being wired to HUD?
Does this prove that diegetic tool UIs are viable in UE5.8 without engine modifications?
Was this derived from Educational_Scanner Q10 (no visual/audio feedback yet) as the gap it fills?
Does the scanner panel conflict with the Verb_Look description overlay (both claim the same HUD region)?
What Blueprint/UMG skills are required to build the scan result panel and targeting reticle?
Does this need sub-sub-features (panel layout, reticle design, knowledge-log integration) or is 26 Qs enough?
Are sibling UI features missing (e.g., Scanner_Scan_Progress, Scanner_History_Log)?
Is the parent Educational_Scanner designed enough to finalize UI questions (Scan() API stable)?
Should the UI panel be built before or after Scanner_Audio_Feedback (visual is primary channel)?
Does the UI block other scanner sub-features, or do other sub-features block it?
Does a beautiful, readable scan panel directly serve 'most famous educational RPG on Steam'?
What development time is sacrificed to polish UI animations vs shipping a simpler text panel?
What evidence shows that diegetic HUD (Dead Space, Metroid Prime) drives more engagement than menu-based info?
Does the UI chain reach PLAYER LEARNING (the terminal) or is it just cosmetic decoration?
